ing: in one piece, or top round
st: Rub the beef with [[1 tsp]] salt. Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and sear the beef on all sides until well browned. Take it out.
Add [[1 tbsp]] butter, the carrots, celery root and onion and cook for [[8 minutes]] until they begin to brown.
Return the beef to the pot with the bay leaves, allspice, peppercorns, cloves and [[2 cups]] broth. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook on low heat, turning the beef halfway, until it is very tender, about 2 hours.
Remove the beef and keep it warm under foil. Discard the bay leaves.
Blend the vegetables and cooking liquid until smooth. Return to the pot and stir in the cream, vinegar, sugar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Simmer 5 minutes.
Slice the beef thickly, pour sauce over it, and serve with bread dumplings and a spoonful of cranberry sauce.

ing: made as in the Knedliky recipe
st: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Rub the pork with [[2 tsp]] salt, the garlic and [[2 tsp]] caraway seeds.
Place the pork in a roasting pan fat side up with [[1 cup]] water. Roast uncovered, basting every 30 minutes with the pan juices.
Check that the pork reaches at least 190°F (88°C) for tender slicing. Rest it under foil for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat [[2 tbsp]] lard in a pot and cook the onion for [[5 minutes]] until golden.
Add the sauerkraut, [[1 tsp]] caraway seeds, the sugar and [[0.5 cup]] water. Simmer partly covered until soft and mellow.
Steam or boil the dumplings and slice them thickly.
Slice the pork, spoon the pan juices over it, and serve with sauerkraut and dumpling slices on each plate.
Toast the bread cubes in a dry pan or the oven until dry and lightly golden.
Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm milk and leave it for 5 minutes until foamy.
In a bowl, mix [[3 cups]] flour with the salt. Add the yeast milk and the eggs and knead for [[6 minutes]] into a smooth, soft dough.
Fold in the toasted bread cubes. Cover and let rise until doubled.
Divide into 2 loaves about 8 inches long and rest them for 10 minutes.
Bring a wide pot of salted water to a gentle boil. Lower in the loaves and cook covered, turning once.
Lift out, prick each loaf with a fork to let steam escape, and slice with thread or a knife. Serve right away.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] lard in a heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onions for [[15 minutes]] until deeply golden and soft.
Stir in the garlic and caraway and cook 1 minute.
Remove the pot from the heat and stir in [[3 tbsp]] paprika and the tomato paste so the paprika does not burn.
Add the beef, [[2 tsp]] salt and the pepper and stir to coat. Pour in the broth and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer on low heat, stirring now and then, until the beef is very tender.
Stir in the marjoram and simmer uncovered for 10 more minutes until the sauce is thick.
Taste for salt and serve with bread dumplings or rye bread.
Stir together the mayonnaise, pickle, capers and lemon juice for a quick tartar sauce. Chill.
Set out three shallow dishes: flour, beaten egg with the salt, and breadcrumbs.
Dip each cheese slab in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs. Repeat egg and crumbs a second time for a thick coat that seals in the cheese.
Freeze the coated cheese for 15 minutes so it holds together while frying.
Heat [[2 cups]] oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the cheese in batches for [[2 minutes]] per side until deep golden, and drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with the tartar sauce and boiled potatoes or a roll.
Grate the potatoes into a bowl, then squeeze them hard in a clean towel to remove as much liquid as you can.
Mix the potatoes with the egg, flour, garlic, marjoram, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Spoon in about [[0.25 cup]] of batter per pancake and flatten into a thin round about 4 inches wide.
Fry for [[4 minutes]] per side until crisp and deep golden. Add oil as needed between batches.
Drain on paper towels and keep warm in a low oven.
Serve hot with sour cream or sauerkraut.
Melt the butter in a pot and cook the mushrooms over medium heat for [[8 minutes]] until browned. Remove half and set aside.
Add the caraway, bay leaf and [[5 cups]] broth and bring to a boil.
Add the potatoes and [[1 tsp]] salt and simmer until the potatoes are tender.
Whisk [[2 tbsp]] flour with the sour cream and cream, then whisk in a ladle of hot soup, then stir it all into the pot. Simmer 5 minutes.
Bring a separate wide pan of water to a gentle simmer and add [[2 tbsp]] vinegar. Crack in the eggs one by one and poach for [[3 minutes]] until the whites are set.
Stir half the dill and [[0.5 tsp]] salt into the soup and remove the bay leaf.
Ladle into bowls, top each with a poached egg, the reserved mushrooms and the remaining dill.
Melt [[1 tbsp]] butter in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion for [[4 minutes]] until soft.
Add the caraway and marjoram and stir for 30 seconds.
Pour in [[5 cups]] broth, add the potatoes, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper, and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer until the potatoes are tender.
Meanwhile, toast the bread cubes in a skillet with [[1 tbsp]] butter until crisp and golden.
Stir the garlic into the soup and cook for only 2 minutes so it stays fresh and sharp.
Ladle into bowls and top with the croutons and the grated cheese.
Mix the drained cheese, egg, salt, semolina and [[1.5 cups]] flour with a fork into a soft dough. Add a spoonful of flour if too sticky.
Rest the dough for 20 minutes covered.
Pit each plum and press a sugar cube inside the cavity.
Roll the dough to 0.25 inch thick on a floured board. Cut into 8 squares and wrap each plum fully, pinching seams tightly and rolling into a ball.
Bring a wide pot of lightly salted water to a gentle boil. Add the dumplings and cook uncovered, stirring gently once.
When they float, cook 2 minutes longer, then lift out with a slotted spoon.
Pour [[4 tbsp]] melted butter over them and sprinkle with [[3 tbsp]] sugar. Serve hot.
Whisk the milk, yeast and [[1 tbsp]] sugar in a bowl and wait 5 minutes until foamy.
Stir in the remaining sugar, [[6 tbsp]] melted butter, 1 egg, the vanilla and salt. Add [[3.5 cups]] flour and knead for [[8 minutes]] into a soft dough.
Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled.
Mix the drained cottage cheese with [[2 tbsp]] sugar for the cheese filling.
Divide the dough into 12 balls, set them on a lined baking sheet, flatten slightly, and let them rise 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Press a deep well in each ball and fill half with jam and half with cheese filling.
Brush the edges with melted butter and bake until golden.
Cool on a rack and dust with powdered sugar.
Mix the warm milk, yeast and [[1 tbsp]] sugar and let stand until foamy.
Add the flour, [[2 tbsp]] sugar, egg yolks, [[4 tbsp]] melted butter and salt and knead for [[8 minutes]] to a smooth dough.
Cover and rise until doubled.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Wrap 6 empty clean cans or rolling pins in foil and grease well.
Roll the dough into a long rope 0.25 inch thick and wind it around each form in a tight spiral, pressing the edges together.
Brush with melted butter and roll in a mix of the remaining sugar and [[1 tbsp]] cinnamon, then bake on a tray until golden.
Roll in the chopped walnuts. Slide the pastry off the forms while warm and serve.

ing: thick pork, such as Czech or kielbasa style
st: Cut the sausages in half lengthwise and cut a few shallow slits in the skin, or peel off the casing if you like.
Layer the sausages, onion rings and bell pepper slices in a large clean jar.
Add the bay leaves, peppercorns and allspice to the jar.
Simmer the vinegar, water, sugar and salt for 3 minutes until the sugar and salt dissolve. Cool for 10 minutes.
Pour the warm brine over the sausages and pour in the oil.
Seal the jar and refrigerate. Turn it over now and then.
Serve cold with dark bread and beer after at least 2 days.
Mix [[4 cup]] flour, [[0.5 cup]] sugar, [[2.25 tsp]] yeast, lemon zest and a pinch of nutmeg.
Add [[1 cup]] warm milk, [[0.5 cup]] melted butter and 2 eggs. Knead 10 minutes until smooth. Knead in the raisins.
Cover and rise 1.5 hours until doubled.
Divide the dough into 9 pieces. Braid a 4-strand base and a 3-strand middle and a 2-strand top, stacking each on the one below.
Place on a lined tray. Rise 45 minutes. Heat the oven to 350°F.
Brush with beaten egg, top with [[0.25 cup]] almonds and bake 40 minutes until deep golden. Cool before slicing.
nt: Best swap: use golden raisins or chopped dried apricots for the raisins at the same amount.
